exposure: Timing of uterine rupture (prelabor vs. during labor)
outcome: Location of rupture (cesarean section scars vs. other)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 69 cases of obstetrical uterine rupture from January 2009 to April 2022 across three tertiary hospitals in South China, categorized by timing of rupture: prelabor (42 cases) and during labor (27 cases).
finding: Uterine ruptures differ significantly by timing, with prelabor ruptures more often involving scars other than CS and placenta percreta at earlier gestational weeks, while ruptures during labor primarily occur after 32 weeks and are strongly linked to TOLAC/VBAC.
mod_finding: Ruptures during labor were strongly associated with Trial of Labor After Cesarean (TOLAC) and identified following Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC).
gest_age: The median gestational age at rupture was 33 weeks for the prelabor group and 39 weeks for the labor group; prelabor ruptures occurred across all gestational intervals, whereas labor-related ruptures mostly occurred after 32 weeks.
